selected.text: The bounty of God is of two kinds: manifest and hidden. The hidden divine bounty, however, is everlasting and unchanging, never to be altered or transformed, for it is the eternal outpouring of God and the perpetual gift of the Lord.
selected.reason: Distinguishes manifest and hidden bounty, adding an explanatory framework.

selected.reason: Qualifies assurance of mercy with the irretrievable opportunity of the present response.

selected.text: We hope that outward means will also be made available, for the divine favors have ever encompassed and continue to encompass all from every direction.
selected.reason: Combines hope in grace with the use of available outward means.

selected.text: O Lord! Have mercy on whoever holds fast to Thee and to Thy verses, and leave him not in the hands of the oppressors among Thy creatures.
selected.reason: Applies divine protection to the vulnerability of people facing oppressors.

selected.text: O my God, my God! Take not Thy servants to task for their grievous transgressions and their great sins. Adorn their heads with the crowns of justice and equity, and illumine their hearts with the light of Thy knowledge, O Thou Who art
selected.reason: Places pardon alongside justice, equity and knowledge as complementary moral qualities.

selected.text: Do good as God hath done good unto thee.
selected.reason: Connects receiving divine goodness with doing good to others.

selected.text: Prevent no one from the ocean of My loving-kindness, and turn not away anyone who has turned to thy luminous countenance
selected.reason: Forbids preventing anyone from approaching the ocean of mercy.

selected.text: These are the days of grace - we look to grace. Were we to look to justice, not a single word would flow from the Pen of the Ancient of Days.
selected.reason: Contrasts strict justice with the gift of revelation and the divine Word.

selected.text: Hadst thou expended all that is on earth, thou wouldst not have attained unto this Tablet. But God doeth whatsoever He willeth, and He is the All-Bountiful, the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful
selected.reason: Distinguishes divine bounty from anything purchasable with material wealth.

selected.text: Today the ocean of mercy is surging and the breezes of forgiveness are wafting from the direction of the favor of the Desire of all worlds. As they pass over receptive souls, all are adorned with the ornament of divine pardon.
selected.reason: Explores receptivity and pardon as a qualification of universal bounty.

selected.text: Had not My mercy preceded all things, I would have returned existence unto non-existence by reason of what hath befallen My loved ones
selected.reason: Portrays mercy restraining destruction amid oppression and rejection.

selected.text: Give thanks to thy Lord, the All-Forgiving, for by His name "The All-Forgiving" He hath forgiven the sins of all the worlds
selected.reason: Extends the prayer for forgiveness across all the worlds of God.

selected.text: at the moment when I gaze upon thee, I see no one possessed of sin upon the face of the earth
selected.reason: Uses a striking personal address concerning sin to explore the reach of forgiveness.

selected.text: O My servants! My remembrance of you is My greatest gift, were you to perceive it.
selected.reason: Identifies remembrance as a supreme gift beyond material bestowals.

selected.text: How many a servant hath been debarred from the choice wine of revelation, and how many a handmaiden hath turned unto it, partaken thereof, and said: "Praise be unto Thee, O God of all worlds!" Verily, grace is in the hand of God; He bestoweth what He willeth upon whom He willeth, and withholdeth from whom He willeth what He desireth. He, verily, is the Almighty, the All-Powerful
selected.reason: Contrasts women receiving the gift with men remaining barred, challenging assumptions of privilege.

selected.text: His loving-kindness hath encompassed all, His mercy hath preceded all things, and He hath created countless means whereby He might lead that honored handmaiden, through the attraction of His call, to the Most Exalted Horizon.
selected.reason: Presents multiple means through which guidance and mercy reach people.

selected.text: Verily thy Lord is the All-Merciful unto the peoples of all worlds, the Compassionate unto all creation, the Forgiving unto the concourse of names, and the Kind unto all who dwell on earth and in heaven.
selected.reason: Connects the manifestations of divine names with bounty throughout creation.

selected.text: His favor hath encompassed the world of existence, both seen and unseen … The forbearance of God, exalted be His glory, seeketh salvation for all. Verily He is the Most Merciful of them that show mercy and the Most Generous of the generous ones
selected.reason: Explains divine forbearance through a wish for the salvation of all.

selected.text: In the Book of God it is recorded that should a person embrace this Faith, his father and mother shall also receive forgiveness.
selected.reason: Preserves a reported application of forgiveness to parents, with its report status explicit.

selected.text: By Thy glory! Even if Thou shouldst punish me with the punishment of Thy power, and enlarge my body to the size of Thy heaven and earth, and burn me in the fire such that no one else is tormented but me - by Thy glory, Thou art the Just One in the sovereignty of Thy grandeur, the One Who is obeyed in the kingdom of Thy oneness, the One Who is praised in all Thy deeds and handiwork, and the One Who is thanked in Thy decrees and ordinations
selected.reason: Adds the Bab's prayerful relation of love and punishment, retaining its hypothetical devotional voice.

selected.text: Oh, trust in God! for His Bounty is everlasting, and in His Blessings, for they are superb. Oh! put your faith in the Almighty, for He faileth not and His goodness endureth for ever! His Sun giveth Light continually, and the Clouds of His Mercy are full of the Waters of Compassion with which He waters the hearts of all who trust in Him.

selected.text: O Lord! We are sinners, but Thou art the Forgiver. We are submerged in the ocean of shortcomings, but Thou art the Pardoner, the Kind. Forgive our sins and bless us with Thine abundant grace. Grant us the privilege of beholding Thy Countenance, and give us the chalice of joy and bliss. We are captives of our own transgressions, and Thou art the King of bountiful favours. We are drowned in a sea of iniquities, and Thou art the Lord of infinite mercy.

selected.text: Regarding your question about forgiveness and pardon for the deceased: Every soul that returns from this transitory world to the eternal realm, according to their merit and capacity - if divine justice encompasses them, "O what regret for us!" But in the realm of grace, merit and capacity and worthiness are not considered. "He forgives whom He wills and pardons whom He wills. Verily He is the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful." After ascension, progress and pardon depend on grace, but descent is impossible and inconceivable. "God transforms evil deeds into good deeds through His grace and pardon and forgiveness." Therefore the seeking of forgiveness by the loved ones and beseeching pardon and forgiveness from the Court of Unity on behalf of the deceased is legitimate and accepted and praiseworthy, and causes abundant pardon and progress. And upon you be greetings and praise.
selected.reason: Explains forgiveness and progress after death through divine grace and supplication.
